item.title: Americans back Social Security, but one-third fear it won’t last
item.description: Most Americans hold a favorable view of Social Security, but about one-third are skeptical the program will still exist when they retire, according to a new survey from the Cato Institute and YouGov.

item.title: Sweeney amends lawsuit against AIME, names UWM
item.description: Katie Sweeney's amended lawsuit against AIME and UWM alleges financial misconduct and contract interference.

item.title: Google enters portal wars with MLS listings in select cities
item.description: Google is testing embedded home listings in mobile search, impacting portal stocks and raising industry questions.

item.title: MRED challenges Zillow’s claims of imminent listing feed disruptions
item.description: MRED disputes Zillow’s warnings of listings disruptions come January, citing no policy violations as of mid-December.

item.title: Inside Pennymac’s Texas expansion and its push for top mortgage talent
item.description: Pennymac CEO David Spector talks about the company's new Texas office, AI investment and Team USA partnership in this Q&A.

item.title: Homebuilder confidence ticks up but remains low
item.description: Builder confidence rose slightly in December but remains low, with 40% of builders cutting prices and 67% offering incentives. Entry-level homebuilders face the greatest challenges due to shrinking margins and weak demand.

item.title: Opendoor names Lucas Matheson president, Christy Schwartz CFO
item.description: Opendoor names Lucas Matheson as president and Christy Schwartz as CFO, aiming to accelerate growth and innovation.

item.title: Florida property insurance market is rebounding from 2022 low point
item.description: The market has rebounded from 2022, when litigation costs, rising losses and multiple insurer failures pushed the system close to collapse.

item.title: Study finds Zillow home estimates improve buyer, seller outcomes
item.description: The availability of a Zestimate increased buyer surplus by nearly 6% on average and raised seller profits by more than 4%.

item.title: PadSplit expands co-living services to 4 new cities
item.description: Founded in 2017, PadSplit operates in more than 35 markets and has listed more than 28,000 rooms, housing 65,000-plus people.
